about: How `-x` tokens bind. A short flag taking a value accepts it attached, attached after `=`, or as the following word. Several value-less shorts may be bundled in one token.

vectors.doc: A short alias sets the flag it belongs to, recorded under the flag's name.
`-j8` binds the rest of the token. mise relies on this for `-C/tmp` and `-Edev`.
An attached value keeps every character after the flag letter, including leading slashes and equals-free punctuation.
`-j=8` binds `8`, not `=8`. A single leading `=` is a separator, matching the long form.
A value-taking short at the end of the command line is an error.
Value-less shorts may share a token: `-ab` sets both.
A bundle may end with a value-taking short, which then consumes the remainder of the token.
An unrecognized letter anywhere in a bundle fails the whole token.

reference.diverges: usage-lib reports `unexpected_arg`: the whole token falls through to positionals, so `-a` is not applied either.

vectors.doc: A `count` flag records how many times it appeared, so `-vvv` is three.
The same count reached through separate tokens gives the same result.
A lone `-` is a value, conventionally meaning stdin, not a flag.
An unrecognized short flag is an error rather than a positional.

reference.diverges: usage-lib binds `-z` to the positional `file`, the same fall-through described in `long-unknown`.
